findings.where: ## Ezekiel 34 and the Good Shepherd, first of the closing lines: If a man who spoke in God's name hurt you, God has already said whose side he is on: "Behold, I am against the shepherds."
findings.problem: (e) A Scripture quotation with no reference beside it. BRIEF.md requires the reference beside every verbatim Scripture quotation. This is a repeat of Ezekiel 34:10, quoted with its reference two paragraphs up (ledger line 129 notes the repeat). The wording itself matches the ESV witness (scratchpad/resv/data/ESV.json); the quotation ends at a period where the verse continues with a comma, which is normal for a truncated quotation.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: If a man who spoke in God's name hurt you, God has already said whose side he is on: "Behold, I am against the shepherds" (Ezekiel 34:10).

findings.where: ## What the Church Did When It Knew, second paragraph: In May 2022 an independent investigation by Guidepost Solutions, which the Convention's messengers had voted for the year before, reported that Executive Committee staff had for years kept a private list of ministers accused of abuse.
findings.problem: (c) The relative clause can read as if the messengers voted for Guidepost Solutions. Ledger line 83, and a WebSearch this run (Baptist Press, 'Guidepost Solutions selected to conduct independent review'; Insurance Journal, 2021-09-21), show that in June 2021 the messengers voted for a third-party investigation overseen by a task force. The task force chose Guidepost in September 2021. The Executive Committee had separately named Guidepost in June, and that review was put on hold. The sentence is true if 'which' attaches to the investigation, but the wording invites the wrong reading.
findings.fix: Replace with: In May 2022 an independent investigation that the Convention's messengers had voted for the year before, carried out by Guidepost Solutions, reported that Executive Committee staff had for years kept a private list of ministers accused of abuse.

findings.where: ## Was Any of It Real?, second paragraph: In North Africa in the early fourth century, after the persecution under the emperor Diocletian, some clergy had handed over copies of Scripture to the authorities to save their lives. A party later called the Donatists held that baptisms and ordinations performed by such men were worthless.
findings.problem: Ambiguous chronology (BRIEF.md lists it as a tell). The handing over happened during the persecution (ledger line 94, WDB NPNF note: 'the persecution in A.D. 303 ... the demand made in that persecution for the surrender of the sacred books'), and the Donatist dispute came after it. As written, 'after the persecution' sits on the handing over.
findings.fix: Replace the two sentences with: In North Africa in the early fourth century, during the persecution under the emperor Diocletian, some clergy handed over copies of Scripture to the authorities to save their lives. When it was over, a party later called the Donatists held that baptisms and ordinations performed by such men were worthless.

findings.where: ## Forgiveness and Reporting, Denhollander paragraph: She told him she forgave him, and that if he ever faced what he had done, the gospel offered him a grace he needed far more than her forgiveness.
findings.problem: (f) A paraphrase of a living person, slightly loose. Ledger line 113 records her words: 'true forgiveness from God which you need far more than forgiveness from me, though I extend that to you as well'. In her statement, what he needed far more than her forgiveness was God's forgiveness, not 'a grace' in general. The present wording joins this with her separate 'grace and hope and mercy' line. It is not unfair, but an exact paraphrase is safer for a living person.
findings.fix: Replace with: She told him she forgave him, and that if he ever faced what he had done, the gospel offered him forgiveness from God, which he needed far more than hers.

findings.where: ## What the Church Did When It Knew, bystanders paragraph: Eli loved his sons, and he did rebuke them. He would not restrain them.
findings.problem: (a) No ledger line. 1 Samuel never says Eli 'loved' his sons. The text says he honored them above God (1 Samuel 2:29, ESV 'honor your sons above me'; BSB 'You have honored your sons more than Me') and did not restrain them (3:13). 'Loved' is a fair reading, but it is stated as fact.
findings.fix: No essay change. Add a ledger line under 'Shiloh': 'Eli loved his sons (What the Church Did When It Knew): the essay's reading of 1 Samuel 2:29 ("honor your sons above me") and 3:13; argument, not a quotation.' If the fixer prefers wording a reader can check in the text, use instead: Eli honored his sons above God (1 Samuel 2:29), and he did rebuke them. He would not restrain them.

findings.where: Opening, second paragraph: Most of the leaders in the public cases have been men, and I will write that way.
findings.problem: (a) A general factual claim with no ledger line. Every case named in the essay (Geoghan, Law, the Southern Baptist accused, Zacharias, Nassar, Eli's sons) supports it, and it gives no figure.
findings.fix: No essay change. Add a ledger line under 'Biography and stance' or a new 'General statements' heading: 'Most of the leaders in the public cases have been men: general characterization, no figure; consistent with every case the essay names (Geoghan, Law, the Southern Baptist accused per the 2019 Chronicle series, Zacharias, Nassar).'

Herman quotation 'All the perpetrator asks is that the bystander do nothing.' WebSearch this run returned the same wording, credited to Trauma and Recovery, on spiritofbosnia.org, cryingoutforjustice.blog, releasechimps.org and sermonaudio.com. Southern Baptist figures (restored 10-27d): WebSearch this run (RNS via bishop-accountability.org, Baptist Standard, Christian Century, the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette via pressreader, FOX 29) gives about 380 church leaders and volunteers accused since 1998 and more than 700 victims. Several outlets say many victims were children, some as young as 3, which supports 'many of them children'. One outlet said 'many of them young men and women', so 'many' (not 'most') is the right word.

Database resistance: WebSearch this run (Baptist News Global on the Guidepost report) says Executive Committee leaders publicly argued that a database of abusers was impossible under local church autonomy while a list was kept. This matches the essay's 'made one impossible' and 'Meanwhile'.

Guidepost timeline: messengers voted in June 2021, the task force chose Guidepost in September 2021, and the report came in May 2022 (WebSearch: Baptist Press, Insurance Journal). The dates are right; see the wording finding above.

Zacharias: WebSearch this run (Christian Post, Eternity News, MinistryWatch, Hope 103.2, bishop-accountability.org) says RZIM hired Miller & Martin, more than a dozen massage therapists were interviewed, and the misconduct spanned years, including accounts described as rape. 'Sexually abused massage therapists over a period of years' and 'investigation commissioned by his own ministry' are supported. He died in May 2020 and the report came in February 2021, as the essay says. He is not a living person.

Law's resignation in December 2002 is per the ledger.

That supports 'She saw no contradiction between the two'. The 2016 public accusation and the January 2018 Michigan courtroom are per the ledger.
